# The component library

Every Part is a file `src/parts/part-NN.tsx` that renders a `Deck` with one component per slide, plus a data file `part-NN.data.ts` with the Part's diagrams, code listings and outputs. Both import from `src/components` (`'../components'`). This page is the API, for the coordinator and for anyone editing a Part by hand.

## A generated Part

```tsx
// Generated by react-slides from slides/part-01-first-agent.md (deck sha256 …, GENERATOR_VERSION 1).
import { B, Code, Cover, Deck, Explain } from '../components';
import { meta, diagrams, listings, outputs } from './part-01.data';

export default function Part01() {
  return (
    <Deck meta={meta} diagrams={diagrams} listings={listings} outputs={outputs}>
      <Cover id="1-001" section="Opening" purpose="…" from={[]} sources={[]} title={<>Agent ตัวแรก</>} />
      <Explain id="1-006" section="1.1 รู้จัก agent" purpose="…" from={["1.1"]} sources={[]}
        title={<>agent คืออะไร</>} body={<>model ที่ <B>เลือกเครื่องมือเอง</B></>}
        visual={{"kind": "diagram", "diagram": "d-agent-loop", "show": ["n-user", "n-model"], "highlight": [], "dim": []}} />
      <Code id="1-011" section="1.2 สร้าง agent" purpose="…" from={["1.2"]} sources={[]}
        title={<>ประกาศ tool</>} body={<>…</>} snippet="1.2-a" lines={[[1, 2], [5, 6]]} highlight={[[5, 5]]} />
    </Deck>
  );
}
```

`Deck` treats each direct child with an `id` prop as one slide, in order. It handles the routes (`#/part-NN/<id>`), the arrow keys, swipes, the progress bar and the saved position.

## Deck and every slide

- `Deck`: `meta: PartMeta`, `diagrams: Record<string, DiagramDef>`, `listings: Record<string, Listing>`, `outputs: Record<string, Block>`, `children`.
- Every layout also takes `Base`: `id` (the deck's slide id), `section` (the section heading, or `Opening` / `Closing`), `purpose`, `from: string[]` and `sources: string[]` (shown as links at the foot of the slide).

## Layouts

Text props are `Rich` (any React content, usually a fragment `<>…</>`). Every prop is required unless marked `?`; TypeScript refuses a slide that misses one.

| Component | Props |
|---|---|
| `Cover` | `title`, `body?`, `visual?` |
| `Focus` | `title`, `body`, `visual` |
| `Explain` | `title`, `body`, `visual` |
| `Steps` | `title`, `items: Rich[]`, `visual` |
| `Compare` | `title`, `left`, `right`, `takeaway`, `leftBlocks?: Block[]`, `rightBlocks?: Block[]` |
| `Code` | `title`, `body`, `notice?`, `snippet: string`, `lines: Range[]`, `highlight: Range[]` |
| `Output` | `title`, `body`, `notice?`, `snippet: string` |
| `Error` | `title`, `cause`, `fix`, `symptom?`, `blocks?: Block[]` |
| `Objectives` | `title`, `items: Rich[]`, `visual?` |
| `Setup` | `title`, `items: Rich[]`, `visual?`, `blocks?: Block[]` |
| `Terms` | `title`, `items: Rich[]`, `visual?` |
| `Question` | `question`, `body`, `items?: Rich[]`, `visual?` |
| `Answer` | `answer`, `why`, `revisit: string` (the slide id to go back to), `visual?` |
| `Practice` | `title`, `task`, `items?: Rich[]` (hints), `solution?` (behind a "show" toggle), `visual?` |
| `Summary` | `title`, `items: Rich[]`, `visual?` |
| `Sources` | `title`, `items: Rich[]` |

- **`Code`** shows the lines `lines` of `listings[snippet]` with their real line numbers, a `⋯` row between ranges, the `highlight` lines marked, and two buttons: copy the shown lines, and copy the whole program. An unverified listing shows its reason as a notice.
- **`Output`** shows `outputs[snippet]` as a terminal block; an `illustrative` block is labelled as example output.
- **`Block`** is `{ lang, info, text }`: a command or a file shown with one copy button.
- **`Visual`** is one of:
  - a diagram state `{ kind: 'diagram', diagram, show, new?, highlight, dim }`: the elements in `show` are drawn, `new` ones draw in when moving forward, `highlight` is stronger and `dim` is faded;
  - `{ kind: 'illustration', key, description, prompt, alt, fallback }`;
  - `{ kind: 'screenshot', key, url, capture, fallback }`.

  An illustration or screenshot shows `src/assets/images/part-NN/<key>.(png|jpg|webp)` when it exists, else the drawing `src/illustrations/part-NN/<key>.tsx`, else its `fallback` (a diagram state, or text).

## Text components

| Component | Renders |
|---|---|
| `P` | a paragraph |
| `Ul`, `Ol`, `Li` | a bulleted or numbered list and its items |
| `B` | bold text |
| `I` | italic text |
| `C` | inline code, with the text as a string: `<C>{"create_agent()"}</C>` |
| `A` | a link that opens in a new tab: `<A href="https://…">text</A>` |

Text that JSX would read (`{ } < > &`, or spaces at the edges) is written as a string expression, `{"a < b"}`, so the page shows it exactly.

## Building blocks

- `SlideFrame`: the frame of every layout: the top line (`Part N · section`), the heading, the body, an optional visual column and the sources. Props: `slide: Base`, `title?`, `children`, `visual?`, `wide?`, `hideSources?`, `titleField?`, `className?`.
- `Field`: `<Field name="body">…</Field>` wraps one field's text and marks it for the check page and the tests.
- `VisualSlot`: `<VisualSlot visual={…} />` renders a `Visual` as above.
- `useDeck()`: inside a slide, the Part's `meta`, `diagrams`, `listings` and `outputs`, the current slide id, the `direction` of the last move (`forward`, `back` or `none`) and `reducedMotion`.

## Sketch primitives

Drawings use rough.js through these components. Each takes `seedKey` (a fixed string: the same key always draws the same wobble), `stroke`, and optionally `strokeWidth`, `fill`, `fillStyle` (`hachure`, `solid`, `zigzag`, `cross-hatch`, `dots`), `roughness`, `dashed` and `className`.

| Component | Shape props |
|---|---|
| `SketchRect` | `x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `rounded?` |
| `SketchEllipse` | `cx`, `cy`, `w`, `h` |
| `SketchLine` | `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2` |
| `SketchPath` | `d` (SVG path data) |
| `SketchArrow` | `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `head?` |

`roleColour` gives the colour of a vocabulary role, such as `roleColour('primary')`. The roles are `primary`, `secondary`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `neutral`; their colours are in `src/theme/roles.ts`.

## Editing a Part by hand

Edit `src/parts/part-NN.tsx` like any React file, then `npm run build` to check it. Keep each slide a direct child of `Deck` with its `id` prop, so navigation and progress keep working.

**Your own slide:** build it on `SlideFrame` and give it the `Base` props.

```tsx
import { type Base, SlideFrame } from '../components';
import { Orbit } from '../my/Orbit';   // your component, in a folder of your own

function OrbitSlide(props: Base) {
  return (
    <SlideFrame slide={props} title={<>ข้อมูลวนอย่างไร</>}>
      <Orbit />
    </SlideFrame>
  );
}

// inside <Deck>, in place of the generated slide:
<OrbitSlide id="1-006" section="1.1 รู้จัก agent" purpose="…" from={[]} sources={[]} />
```

**Wrapping a generated slide,** for example in an animation: the wrapper takes the layout's props and passes them on, so it keeps the `id`.

```tsx
import type { ComponentProps } from 'react';
import { Explain } from '../components';

function Spotlight(props: ComponentProps<typeof Explain>) {
  return <div className="my-spotlight"><Explain {...props} /></div>;
}

// replace <Explain … /> with <Spotlight … />, keeping every prop
```

Put your own components and styles in folders the skill does not write to, such as `src/my/`.

**What happens on the next run:** the skill records the hash of every file it writes. A file that no longer matches is yours: it is skipped from then on and listed in the report with what the new version would change. A Part's `.tsx` and `.data.ts` are skipped together, so the code shown never drifts from the deck. To take the skill's version again, run `build_part.py` with `--force <path>`. `src/course.ts` is written once and never touched again. Template files (`src/components/`, `src/theme/`) follow the same rule: an edit is kept, and the report lists it when an upgrade would change that file.

The component API only grows within a template major version: props may be added, never renamed or removed.

Problems with a component or with this page go in `<course_dir>/web/_work/part-NN/skill-problems.md`, as `SKILL.md` describes.
